title: PPC-spiral measurement infrastructure
description:
Cross-cutting infrastructure that must land before any kernel work in the gf2-core PPC-spiral epic. Establishes the pinned baseline, the geomean-comparison harness, the asm-artefact convention, and the proptest equivalence helper.

## Background

The PPC methodology requires four pieces of infrastructure to enforce proof-of-gain at every spiral step: (1) a pinned criterion baseline so before/after measurements compare against a stable reference, (2) a geomean-comparison harness that exits non-zero if a kernel falls below the $1.5\times$ bar, (3) an asm-artefact convention so reviewers can confirm the expected mnemonics actually emitted, and (4) a proptest helper that proves bit-exact equivalence between scalar and SIMD paths.

This story has four child tasks: I1 pins baselines, I2 adds the compare harness and registers the `criterion-1.5x` gate, I3 adds the asm-regen script and registers the `asm-artefact-present` gate, I4 adds the proptest scaffolding. Without all four landed, no downstream tier task can prove its gain.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] `dev/benchmarks/ppc-baselines.json` exists, valid JSON, contains an entry for every Tier A–D kernel with `baseline_name`, `commit_hash`, `bench_target`.
- [hard] `dev/benchmarks/ppc-compare.sh <kernel-id>` exits 0 if geomean speedup $\geq 1.5\times$, else exits 1 with a diff table.
- [hard] JIT gates `criterion-1.5x` and `asm-artefact-present` are registered in the gate registry.
- [hard] Proptest helper at `crates/gf2-core/tests/simd_equiv/mod.rs` compiles and is unit-tested with a trivial SIMD/scalar pair (the existing `LogicalFns::xor_fn`).

## Notes

Word-boundary lengths to test: `[0, 1, 63, 64, 65, 127, 128, 129, 255, 256, 257]`. Helper covers unaligned slice offsets 0..7 within an over-allocated buffer.
